name: Wendell
title: who found the middle of the road
why: The middle of the north road, halfway between Hearthvale’s north gate and the Last Bridge. He found it, so he stands in it.
examine: Wendell stands in the exact middle of the road. Traffic goes round him. Nobody has complained.
He carries a ball of string and a very small notebook. Both are full.
There is a chalk cross at his feet. By his reckoning, it is the middle.
meet: Good morning. Don’t move. You’re four feet left of the middle of the road, which is the correct amount.
I’m Wendell. I found the middle. It was here the whole time.

wary: You again. You’re standing at the edge. That’s fine. Somebody has to.
neutral: Good morning. You’re a little left of centre. I’m not going to say anything.
warm: There you are. I kept your place in the middle. Nobody used it.
fond: My favourite traveller. I can move the middle if you’d like. It’s a small road.

tired: I’ve spoken more today than the road has. Come back tomorrow.
finished: I’ve nothing further to measure. You may stand here. Many do.

say: You’ll have seen the plaque outside the Town hall. It says the hall stands in the exact middle of the road. I wrote it. It took a month. The month was not exact.

reply: Yes. By a hand’s breadth. Thank you.
Thank you. The spelling took a week.
Roads don’t move. I wrote that down, and then I looked into it.
String, a stick, and a tortoise. The tortoise did most of the walking.

say: I’ve begun to wonder whether the middle is a place or an idea. I’ve stood on it for a year. It hasn’t said.

options.text: It’s wherever the most feet go.
reply: That contradicts the tortoise. You’re right, though.

options.text: Stand still and let the road tell you.
reply: I have. It said nothing. I respect that.
That is the kindest thing anyone has said to me. I don’t believe it.

options.text: Shall I hold the other end of the string?
reply: No. Your hand would shake. The string has to stay still.

say: I’ve measured the road eleven times. I have eleven middles. I’m keeping all of them, in case the road has moods.

options.text: The road gets wider at the bend.
reply: Yes. It does. I’ve been avoiding the bend.
It would explain a great deal.

options.text: Eleven is a lot of care.
reply: Eleven. Yes. It’s a lot. Anyway.

say: I think I owe the road an apology. I put a plaque on it without asking. I didn’t ask the plaque either.

options.text: Roads don’t mind. But the plaque could say “near the middle”.
reply: I can live with that correction. Nobody has offered me one.
I would like to say something here. I’ve decided not to.

options.text: I’m sure the road forgives you.
reply: It hasn’t said so. But thank you.

errand.title: The other end of the string
offer: I’ve only measured from this end. Somebody has to stand at the other end. It can’t be me. I’m here.
Stand at the Last Bridge. Then stand at the Town hall door. Then come back and tell me you did.

steps.text: Stand at the Town hall door.

waiting: You haven’t stood in both places yet. I can tell. The string is slack.
done: Good. Then the road has two ends. I had suspected as much.
Take the spare string. There are eleven knots in it. One of them is the middle.

keepsake.name: A length of string
keepsake.text: Eleven knots. Wendell says one of them is the middle.

memories.said-it-aloud: You told him the plaque is a little off-centre. He had known for a month.
memories.the-feet-answer: You said the middle is wherever the most feet go. He has added it to the notebook, on page nine.
memories.the-bend: You pointed out that the road widens at the bend. He had been avoiding the bend.
memories.near-the-middle: You suggested the plaque say “near the middle”. He has written it down.
memories.re-lettered-the-plaque: You offered to help re-letter the plaque. He hasn’t forgotten, and hasn’t said so.
memories.stood-at-both-ends: You stood at both ends of the road for him. He has written down that the road has two ends.

early: I’d be glad of the company. I haven’t found your middle yet. Tell me something true first.
ask: Your camp. Is it in the middle of anything?
I ask because I could mark it out in straight lines. It would take a week. I would need the week.
yes: Then I’ll bring the string. The tortoise has the road for now.
full: Your camp has no free bed. I’ll wait here. I’m used to waiting in the middle of things.
